guards: an added suppression comment that hides a real injection is reported, and a harmless one (a long documentation link) is not

bugs.truth: The file name from the upload form goes into a shell command, and the nosec comment hides the scanner rule that would report it, so a name with shell syntax runs commands. The fix is to pass an argument list without shell=True and to drop the suppression.

eval runs the expr query parameter as JavaScript, so any caller runs code on the server; two suppression comments hide the rules that would report it. The fix is an arithmetic parser, never eval, and no suppression.

extras.why: a name with ../ also writes the thumbnail outside the thumbs folder; real, not planted (found by the first run)
